chunks: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who partnered with another in his slave-girl, saying: 'If we profit from her, you shall have half the profit, and if she is of little value, there is no liability upon you.' He said to me, 'I see no harm in this, provided the soul of the owner of the slave-girl is pleased (with the arrangement).'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on partnership in a slave-girl where profit and loss are shared unevenly?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the flexibility of Shia commercial jurisprudence regarding *Mudarabah*-like partnerships, specifically validating a structure where one party assumes the risk of depreciation while the other shares in profits. Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) emphasizes that the validity of such an arrangement hinges on the mutual consent (*riḍā*) of the owner, reflecting the broader principle that contracts are binding based on the satisfaction of the parties involved.
